lessonRef.subject: mathematics
lessonRef.title: Discussion or problem seminar: comparing extreme quantities

sections.title: Instructional examples
sections.directions: One approach is shown. There is at least one other that works.

steps: A larger power of ten always makes a number larger when the coefficient is between 1 and 10.

sections.title: Guided practice
sections.directions: For each, name a second method before you solve it.

items.prompt: Multiply (6 × 10^-2) × (9 × 10^2) and write the result in scientific notation.
A processor performs 9 × 10^7 operations per second. How many operations does it perform in 6 × 10^1 seconds? Write the answer in scientific notation.
A cell has a diameter of about 5 × 10^2 meters. A virus has a diameter of about 1 × 10^-1 meters. How many times as large is the cell as the virus?

sections.title: Independent practice
sections.directions: Work on your own. Show the steps that produced each answer.

items.prompt: A student claims 9^0 = 0. Which statement best analyzes the claim?
choices: The claim is incorrect; any nonzero base raised to the power 0 equals 1, so 9^0 = 1.
The claim is correct; anything to the power 0 is 0.
The claim is incorrect; 9^0 is undefined.

items.prompt: A student multiplies (3 × 10^0) × (9 × 10^0) and writes 27 × 10^0. Which statement best analyzes the claim?
choices: The exponents should have been multiplied: 27 × 10^0.
The claim is correct and already in scientific notation.
The value is correct but not in scientific notation; 27 × 10^0 should be rewritten as 2.7 × 10^1.
The coefficients should have been added, not multiplied: 12 × 10^0.

sections.title: Extension and challenge
sections.directions: Argue for one method over another. Say what makes it better, not just that it is.

items.responseExpectation: Give the result and the reasoning that produced it. Show enough work that someone else could check each step.
Give the result and the reasoning that produced it. Show enough work that someone else could check each step.
